ing: very fresh tuna or mahi mahi
previously frozen sushi-grade, cut into small cubes
st: Cut the fish into 0.5 inch cubes with a very sharp knife. Keep it cold at all times.
Put the fish in a glass or ceramic bowl. Pour the lime juice over, add [[0.5 tsp]] salt and stir so every piece is covered.
Cover and chill in the fridge until the fish turns opaque and firm on the outside, about 30 minutes. Raw fish carries some risk, so buy the best quality from a trusted fishmonger.
Meanwhile, dice the onion, tomato and cucumber.
Drain off about half of the lime juice from the fish.
Fold in the onion, tomato, cucumber, chili and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Stir in the chilled coconut milk right before serving. Taste and add salt or lime if needed. Serve cold in bowls or coconut shells.

ing: fresh or frozen and thawed, stems removed
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
Wash the taro leaves well and pat dry. Taro leaves must be cooked thoroughly, never eaten raw.
Stir the onion, lime juice and salt into the coconut milk.
Layer several taro leaves in a deep dish or on a large sheet of foil, forming a cup shape.
Spoon some of the coconut mixture into the center. Fold the leaves over to make a bundle.
Repeat to use all the leaves and filling. Pour any leftover coconut mixture on top.
Wrap tightly with foil or banana leaf and bake until the leaves are very tender and silky.
Open carefully because of the steam. Serve hot as a side with fish or rice.

ing: or regular taro root, peeled and cut in chunks
st: Wear gloves if you can, since raw taro can irritate skin. Peel the taro and cut it into 2-inch chunks.
Put it in a pot with [[8 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and cook until completely soft when pierced with a knife. Taro must be fully cooked.
Drain well and return to the pot.
Mash the taro roughly with a masher.
Warm the coconut milk with the sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Stir the coconut milk mixture into the mash until creamy.
Fold in the grated coconut and serve warm.
Rub a little oil on your hands and knife, since breadfruit sap is sticky. Peel the breadfruit, cut it in quarters and remove the core.
Slice the flesh as thinly as you can, about 1/8 inch thick.
Soak the slices in [[4 cups]] cold water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 10 minutes. Drain well and pat completely dry.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 340°F (170°C).
Fry in small batches, stirring, until golden and crisp, about 4 minutes. Keep batches small so the oil stays hot.
Lift out and drain on paper towels.
Toss while hot with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the chili powder. Serve with lime wedges.

ing: or Dungeness or other large crab, live and fresh
st: Use a crab that is alive and fresh. Chill it in the freezer for 15 minutes first to make it sleepy.
Bring [[2 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a large pot with a rack or steamer basket.
Add the crab, cover tightly, and steam until the shell is bright orange-red and the meat is opaque.
Meanwhile, simmer the coconut milk with the garlic over low heat for 10 minutes.
Stir the lime juice into the coconut sauce and keep warm.
Remove the crab and let it rest 5 minutes, then crack the claws and shell.
Serve with the warm coconut-garlic sauce and lime wedges for dipping.

ing: peeled, cored and cut in chunks
st: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a baking dish with the butter.
Boil the breadfruit chunks in [[6 cups]] water until very soft and easy to mash.
Drain well and mash until smooth.
Warm the coconut milk with the sugar and salt until dissolved.
Mix the coconut milk into the mashed breadfruit, then fold in half of the grated coconut.
Spread in the dish and sprinkle with the remaining coconut.
Bake until firm and lightly golden on top.
Let it cool for 15 minutes, then slice or spoon out. Serve warm or cold.
